name: Fader, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the 2017 Act's Subsection (d) was an ordinary statute of limitations, not a statute of repose, and therefore the 2023 Act's retroactive elimination of it is constitutional as it did not abrogate vested rights.

name: Biran, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the 2017 Act's Subsection (d) was clearly a statute of repose, which creates vested rights that cannot be retroactively abrogated by the 2023 Act without violating the Maryland Constitution, and that the majority failed to interpret the 2017 Act as written.

name: Eaves, J.
description: Dissented, joined Justice Biran's and Justice McDonald's opinions.

name: McDonald, Robert N.
description: Dissented, joined Justice Biran's opinion and further argued that the majority's interpretation renders Subsection (d) meaningless and improperly discounts the significance of the bill's title.

name: Graeff, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the State's nolle prosequi was void because it circumvented the victim's right to appeal, and the circuit court violated the victim's rights to sufficient notice and in-person attendance at the vacatur hearing.

name: Berger, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the appeal was moot due to the State's nolle prosequi, and that the victim's rights to notice and attendance were satisfied by electronic participation, even if the notice period was short.

name: Watts, J.
description: Concurred, argued that trial counsel's failure to object to the no-communication order constituted an actual denial of assistance of counsel, presuming prejudice under the Sixth Amendment and Maryland Declaration of Rights.

name: Biran, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Majority was correct to base its holding on Articles 21 and 24 of the Maryland Declaration of Rights, even without full briefing, due to the Supreme Court's failure to conclusively answer the Sixth Amendment question.

name: Fader, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Appellate Court's decision should be affirmed under federal constitutional law and that the Majority improperly ruled on Maryland constitutional law without proper briefing.

name: Gould, J.
description: Dissented, argued that prejudice should not be presumed for ineffective assistance of counsel claims unless the defendant proves actual deprivation, which requires showing a desire to communicate with counsel.

name: FADER, C.J.
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that the statute is constitutional and emergency circumstances existed.

name: BIRAN, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that while the statute is constitutional, the specific October 1 start date for canvassing might not have been strictly necessary for planning, emphasizing that remedies must be narrowly tailored.

name: Robert N. McDonald
description: Concurred, arguing that petitioners did not provide compelling evidence of constitutional violations and the Court's role is limited to assessing compliance, not creating a "better" plan.

name: Joseph M. Getty
description: Dissented, arguing that the legislative redistricting plan was an "extreme partisan gerrymander" due to lack of compactness and transparency, and that the Court failed its constitutional duty to ensure fair districts.

name: Gould, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority misapplied legislative privilege and burdens of proof, and the State should have been compelled to disclose information on the map-drawing process.

name: Biran, J.
description: Dissented, joining Chief Judge Getty's and Judge Gould's dissenting opinions.

name: McDonald, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the original sentencing court, unaware of subsequent Supreme Court precedents, could not have properly determined if Malvo was constitutionally eligible for life without parole, thus requiring resentencing.

name: Watts, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Circuit Court essentially complied with Miller by considering Malvo's youth and attendant circumstances, and that Jones v. Mississippi supports that an explicit finding of permanent incorrigibility is not required.

name: Hotten, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Malvo's sentences were just, fair, and compliant with the Constitutions, as the sentencing court had discretion, considered mitigating factors like youth, and the crimes warranted life without parole. Also argued JUVRA cures any alleged deficiencies.

name: Gould, J.
description: Dissented, argued that he joins the dissenting opinions of Watts, J. and Hotten, J.

name: Gould, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the student member position is a legislative creation, not an elective office subject to the Maryland Constitution's election and voting requirements.

name: Glenn T. (Senior Judge, Specially Assigned), J.
McDonald, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Chief Judge acted within her authority to issue the administrative tolling order during the pandemic, as it did not usurp other branches' powers or violate the Maryland Declaration of Rights.

name: BIRAN, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the trial court violated Leidig's confrontation rights under Article 21 by admitting a scientific report without the opportunity for cross-examination of its author, establishing a new 'primary purpose' standard for determining if such reports are testimonial.

name: Getty, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the tax setoff statutes are constitutional because they do not regulate matters of purely local concern and their broad effect on county residents means they do not fall under the uniformity requirement of Article XI-E, § 1.
